facts.text: PyPDM controls AlphANOV PDM laser sources, supports PDM protocol version 3.4 to 3.7 and lets daisy-chained devices share one serial link

The documentation lists the PDM properties that can be read or changed: sync source, delay line type, frequency, pulse width, delay, offset current, current percentage, current, temperature, maximum current, current source, interlock status, activation and mode
The link opens the serial port at 125000 baud and frames a command as length, address, command id, data and a checksum
The checksum is the XOR of the frame bytes minus one, modulo 256
A response is a length byte, a status byte, the data and a checksum; a status other than OK raises StatusError
The PDM constructor validates the protocol version: major 3 and minor 4 to 7
The class states its bounds: MAX_DELAY 15000 ps, MAX_PULSE_WIDTH 1275000 ps and MAX_FREQUENCY 250000000 Hz
The offset current setter refuses a value below 0 or above 150 mA
The current percentage setter refuses a value below 0 or above 100
The current in mA is current_percentage times maximum_current divided by 100
The maximum pulse current and the maximum mean current are read from the device and cached
InterlockStatus.CLOSED is 0 (the laser can pulse) and InterlockStatus.OPEN is 1 (it cannot pulse)
The mode command reads the continuous or pulsed hardware switch: 0 for pulsed and 1 for continuous
The activation is a boolean instruction and apply() makes the pending instructions effective
apply() sends the APPLY_ALL_INSTRUCTIONS command, which makes all settings in volatile memory effective
The destructor sets the activation to False and calls apply() for safety
The synchronization sources are EXTERNAL_TTL_LVTTL 0, EXTERNAL_LVDS 1 and INTERNAL 2; the delay line types are NONE 0 and INTERNAL 1; the current sources are ANALOG 0 and NUMERIC 1
